# homeassistant_user (Resource)

A Home Assistant user, optionally with a username and password to log in with. The owner and system-generated users cannot be managed. Changing the username or password of an existing user needs the token of the owner, not only of an admin. Create a `homeassistant_person` with this user's `id` to track the user's presence.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A user who logs in with a username and password, and the person that tracks them.
resource "homeassistant_user" "jane" {
  name     = "Jane"
  username = "jane"
  password = var.jane_password
  group    = "user"
}

resource "homeassistant_person" "jane" {
  name            = "Jane"
  user_id         = homeassistant_user.jane.id
  device_trackers = ["device_tracker.jane_phone"]
}

# With OpenTofu or Terraform 1.11 or later, a write-only password stays out of the state. Bump
# password_wo_version to set a new one.
resource "homeassistant_user" "john" {
  name                = "John"
  username            = "john"
  password_wo         = var.john_password
  password_wo_version = 1
}

# A user without a password login, e.g. for a wall tablet that logs in with a token.
resource "homeassistant_user" "wall_tablet" {
  name       = "Wall tablet"
  group      = "read-only"
  local_only = true
}

variable "john_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "jane_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `group` (String) What the user may do: `admin`, `user` (the default), or `read-only`.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the user can log in. Defaults to `true`.
- `local_only` (Boolean) Whether the user can log in only from the local network. Defaults to `false`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password to log in with. It is kept in the state, so protect the state. Home Assistant cannot report the password, so a change made outside OpenTofu is not detected. Creating a login needs it or `password_wo`. Without either, the provider leaves the password of an existing login as it is, e.g. after an import. Changing the password of an existing login needs the owner's token. Needs `username`. To keep the password out of the state, use `password_wo` instead.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password to log in with, as a write-only attribute: OpenTofu passes it to the provider but never stores it in the plan or state. Needs OpenTofu or Terraform 1.11 or later; with older versions, use `password`. Because the provider cannot see a change of a write-only value, it sets the password when the login is created and whenever `password_wo_version` changes. Changing the password of an existing login needs the owner's token. Needs `username`.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Any number that changes when `password_wo` changes, e.g. `1`, then `2`. Changing it sets the password from `password_wo`.
- `username` (String) Username to log in with. It must be lowercase and have no spaces at the start or end. Without it, the user has no password login. Removing it from the configuration deletes the login; the plan warns about it. Changing it renames the login in place and needs the owner's token. Creating a login needs `password` or `password_wo`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) User ID that Home Assistant assigned, a random hex string. Import with this ID or with the username.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a user by its ID, or by its username. Keep `username` in the configuration of a user
# who has one: without it, the next apply deletes the login (the plan warns). Without `password`,
# the login keeps its password; with it, the next apply sets it.
tofu import homeassistant_user.jane 0f8e2c4a6b1d4e3f9a7c5b2d8e6f1a3c
tofu import homeassistant_user.jane jane
```
